editorial.headline: Health Support Services: Open Nationally, Scope-Sensitive in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A broad health-support activity that is fully foreign-open nationally, but whose Bali registration outcome depends on the precise scope and risk declared in OSS.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the health-support infrastructure behind clinical care, whether managed by government or private operators. Its scope includes blood-management units, medical and public-health laboratories, optometry providers, diagnostic centres, stem-cell and/or cell-processing laboratories, eye banks, plasma banks, cell or tissue banks, biobanks, biorepositories, precision-medicine facilities, genetic testing and analysis laboratories, hearing-assistance centres, optical services, and other medical-support services. It is a deliberately wide category: the common thread is not one clinical specialty, but the systems, facilities and specialist services that enable health assessment, analysis, storage and support.

Registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That national position is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the important reading is straightforward: this is not a nationally reserved activity, and the record permits full foreign ownership within the stated national framework.

Bali requires a more exact reading. The provincial position is not an automatic block, but it is scope-sensitive: at Besar scale, some activities within this broad grouping are low risk in OSS while others carry a higher risk. A PMA registration in Bali is possible only where the higher-risk scope is declared, and the exact activity must be verified live in OSS. This matters because Bali permanently blocks PMA for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island. The practical conclusion is neither a blanket yes nor a blanket no. The national foreign-investment position remains fully open, but in Bali the viability of a PMA registration turns on the precise service being registered and its live OSS risk classification.
